title: The independent reading of the commercial-overlay text captured in step P2, written into the R6B reference cases: two readings from a sealed folder, a value only where both agree (gap K9; D-090 R226, R241, R259, R291, R318)
objective: Read the commercial-overlay text captured by task M4-T026 independently, and write what the readings settle into the R6B reference cases (docs/plans/R6B_RESULTS_CONNECTION_WORK_ORDER_2026-10-06.md, section 5 gap K9 and section 8: 'capture the missing law text, then read it independently'; the work order withholds every residential result on a lot with a recorded overlay until this reading exists). INPUT MADE BY THE ORCHESTRATOR BEFORE THE BUILDER STARTS: two readings by two different AI helpers that took no part in writing the program's rules, each working alone from a sealed folder (every pinned law capture without its notes, the benchmark lot's recorded official facts and outline, no floor-area-ratio field, no program output) and with no access to the program or the repository. The readings cover, for a residential building on a lot where a C2-2 overlay is mapped within an R6B district (the benchmark lot) and for the same lot without the overlay: (1) which district's residential bulk regulations ZR 34-111 and ZR 34-11 make applicable, and what they route to; (2) the height and setback route of ZR 34-24, ZR 35-63, 35-631, 35-632 and 35-633 for a district with R6B equivalency, and whether it changes the base heights, the building height or the setback the R6B table and ZR 23-433 give; (3) the street-wall location rule of ZR 35-631 and whether its conditions are met or not known for the lot; (4) the rear-yard provision of ZR 35-53 and to which buildings its own words apply; (5) whether any captured overlay text changes the floor area ratio, the lot coverage or the dwelling-unit limit; (6) every section the texts point to that is not captured, and what stays not known because of it. THE BUILDER then: saves the two returns unchanged under docs/reference-cases/R6B/provenance/; adds a case (or rows) for the overlay reading in which a value or a yes/no is recorded only where BOTH readings give it on the same basis, and everything else is 'not known' with the reason and both readings named; updates the real-lot rows that an overlay bears on only by adding the overlay reading beside them with a recorded reason (no expected value changes unless both readings support the change); corrects the sentence about lots of 30,000 sq ft or more in the interior-lots case to what the captured ZR 23-362(b) says (backlog row DB-168), with a change-log entry; updates the README; re-renders the pages; extends the test support only as the new rows need. Nothing in a case comes from a program run. No rule file, rule engine, capture, register entry, plan or screen changes.
business_reason: Gap K9: the benchmark lot has a recorded C2-2 overlay, so the work order shows nothing for it until the governing sections are captured (done, task M4-T026) and read independently (this task). Step 3 of the owner's eight steps (R291) and the owner's rule that interpretation is checked with independently worked, source-backed examples kept apart from program output (R226, R241, R259, R318).
